questions.question_text: In computer graphics, which visual format uses mathematical equations to define lines and shapes, ensuring the image can be scaled infinitely without losing quality?
Which traditional printmaking technique relies on a physical matrix where the non-printing areas are carved away, leaving the design raised on the surface?
In typography and calligraphy layout, what is the term used to describe the adjustable spacing between individual characters in a word?
During the three-dimensional clay sculpting process, what is the primary structural purpose of an 'armature'?
options: A) To add final color to the fired clay
B) To act as a rigid internal framework supporting the heavy wet clay mass
C) To smooth the outer texture of the sculpture
D) To create a protective glaze layer
questions.answer: B) To act as a rigid internal framework supporting the heavy wet clay mass

sections.section_name: Section B - Theory Short Answer Concepts

questions.question_text: Describe the fundamental differences between additive and subtractive methods in three-dimensional sculptural design. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: The additive method involves building up forms by adding material, like layering wet clay. The subtractive method involves removing material from a solid block, such as carving marble or wood, to reveal the form.

questions.question_text: Explain the concept of 'visual hierarchy' when designing an effective typographic poster layout. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Visual hierarchy organizes typographic elements by scale, weight, and color to guide the viewer's eye sequentially. It ensures critical information, like the headline, is processed first, followed by supporting details.

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of a 'registration mark' in multi-color stencil and relief printmaking workflows? [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Registration marks are precise alignment guides used to ensure that each successive layer or color block in a print aligns perfectly with the previous layers, preventing blurred or overlapping image errors.

questions.question_text: Outline the basic material differences between a traditional paper collage and a mixed-media mask craft. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Collage strictly adheres flat paper or fabric elements onto a two-dimensional surface. Mask craft is a three-dimensional process combining structural bases like papier-mâché with varied materials like feathers, beads, and wire.

questions.question_text: Define the role of 'white space' or negative space in computer graphic design compositions. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: White space provides breathing room around active visual elements. It prevents graphic clutter, enhances readability in typography, and creates a balanced, professional aesthetic composition in digital layouts.

sections.section_name: Section C - Practical Composition & Design Layouts

questions.question_text: Formulate a structural layout and scoring rubric for a multi-layered stencil print project themed 'Urban Architecture'. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: The layout requires a minimum of three distinct, hand-cut stencil layers representing foreground, midground, and background architectural silhouettes. Scoring benchmarks evaluate edge sharpness, accurate registration alignment between layers, and the effective use of contrasting ink values to create depth.

questions.question_text: Draft the procedural steps and compositional margins for designing an illuminated calligraphy quotation poster in a Gothic script style. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: The composition must establish calculated border margins framing a centered text block. Scoring will assess consistent x-height and ascender/descender ratios in the Gothic lettering, uniform ink flow, and the integration of intricate, balanced illuminated borders wrapping the primary quotation.

questions.question_text: Design a practical evaluation matrix for a 3D clay relief sculpture based on a 'Floral Motif' pattern. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: The relief must demonstrate varying depths carved into a flat clay slab. Scoring focuses on structural integrity, the smooth transition between high and low relief elements, intricate textural detailing of petals and leaves, and the absence of air pockets.

sections.section_name: Section D - Applied Art Portfolios & Digital Synthesis

questions.question_text: Detail the vector graphics workflow required to digitize and vectorize a hand-drawn logo sketch for an Art Integrated Project Portfolio. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Begin by scanning the hand-drawn sketch at high resolution and importing it into the vector software as a locked background layer. Next, use the pen tool to trace the sketch with precise anchor points and bezier curves. Finally, convert strokes to scalable paths, apply solid digital color fills, and organize the final graphic into organized, labeled layers.

questions.question_text: Construct a curation strategy for compiling a cohesive physical Art Portfolio that transitions from traditional printmaking to applied digital poster design. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The portfolio curation must demonstrate a clear evolutionary narrative. It should open with foundational, handmade relief prints showcasing understanding of positive/negative space. The middle section should present scanned, digitized versions of these prints. The portfolio concludes with applied designs, integrating the digital prints into fully formatted typographic posters, proving the student's ability to synthesize traditional crafts with computer graphics.
